text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary release r-2026.03.17 -> runtime-pool-7: sudden latency spike and throughput drop detected. p50=180ms p95=1.2s p99=2.4s, overall throughput -40%, kernel_fallback_rate=23%. Affected hosts: rp-7-{a,b,c}. Auto-fallback engaged. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/3491112222
clara_oncall: oncall here. I'm paging runtime and ops. tagging @bob_runtime @alice_ops. Is there an active rollback/kill-switch?
bob_runtime: ack, looking at traces now. I see a batching config change in the canary: batch_max_tokens bumped to 2048 yesterday. Kernel fallback spikes line up with increased sequence windows.
alice_ops: confirmed, the release included "adaptive_batch_threshold" toggle. Canary config shows threshold lowered too far causing larger mixed-batch fanout.
dave_sre: paging SRE. Are customer-facing 5xxs happening or only latency? We need impact assessment.
eve_pm: Product: three customers reported request timeouts (5xx) in the last 10m, support ticket counts doubled. No broad page for paying customers yet but this is user-visible.
bob_runtime: logs: ```ERROR runtime-worker rp-7-a - kernel_fallback=true kv_cache_miss=0.42 batch_size=1->8 seq_len=1536``` Looks like small requests are being forced into large execution path due to batching threshold misclassification. KV cache churn increased.
clara_oncall: mitigation options: 1) flip canary kill-switch to stop traffic to r-2026.03.17, 2) flip adaptive_batch_threshold back to previous value, 3) rollback the canary image. Which is lowest risk?
alice_ops: quickest is feature-flag flip. Endpoint: `POST https://ops-api.internal/flags/adaptive_batch_threshold` payload: `{"value":"legacy","target":"r-2026.03.17"}`. I can run, will take effect on new sessions immediately, existing in-flight may still hit fallback.
bob_runtime: flag flip first, then roll back if metrics don't recover in 5-7m. Also suggest temporarily increase batching_timeout_ms to reduce micro-batching frenzy: `kubectl patch configmap runtime-config -n prod --type merge -p '{"data":{"batching_timeout_ms":"25"}}'`
clara_oncall: do the flag flip now please. Alice, authorize.
alice_ops: executing flag flip now. ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"value":"legacy","target":"r-2026.03.17"}' https://ops-api.internal/flags/adaptive_batch_threshold```
deploy-bot: [ACTION] Feature flag adaptive_batch_threshold set to "legacy" for target r-2026.03.17 by alice_ops at 3491112350.
bob_runtime: seeing partial recovery: p95 down to 420ms, p99 780ms, throughput still -20%. Kernel fallback rate dropped to 11%. KV miss trending down.
eve_pm: noting customer tickets updating to "improved". still tracking 2 open high-priority tickets.
dave_sre: if we don't hit baseline in next 10m, start rollback. Clara, can you prepare rollback command?
clara_oncall: preparing rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/runtime-serving -n prod --to-revision=2026-03-16-rc3` Will coordinate window to avoid double-deploy.
alice_ops: I'll standby, will trigger rollback on your go. also prepping incident ticket and customer comms draft.
clara_oncall: go for rollback in 4m if no further recovery.
bob_runtime: metrics at +6m: p95 210ms, p99 330ms, throughput -5%. Looks like flag flip mostly mitigated. Kernel fallback at 3%. Recommend hold rollback.
dave_sre: agree. Keep kill-switch in place for the canary and monitor. We'll keep the canary removed from traffic routing for now: `route-manage remove-target --pool runtime-pool-7 --target r-2026.03.17`
deploy-bot: [ROUTE] Removed target r-2026.03.17 from runtime-pool-7 by clara_oncall at 3491112610.
eve_pm: customer comms sent to impacted customers: "We detected elevated latency and have routed your traffic away from the canary. We're monitoring and will follow up."
clara_oncall: handing off to daytime SRE team for monitoring and postmortem: tagging @dave_sre and @bob_runtime for tomorrow's RCA. I'm heading offline.
dave_sre: taking over monitoring. Action items: 1) rollback avoided, flag reverted for canary, keep target removed, 2) collect heap/kv cache metrics for rp-7 hosts, 3) add a guard in rollout job to prevent adaptive_batch_threshold <= 512 without perf sign-off.
bob_runtime: note for RCA: root cause likely bad default for adaptive batching thresholds + lack of canary isolation for kernel selection heuristics. Will gather traces and sample requests.
alice_ops: incident ticket created: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-3491112222 - assigned to eng-runtime. Draft RCA and customer impact summary in ticket.
eve_pm: thanks team. I'll coordinate customers and update support.
clara_oncall: final: incident mitigated, kill-switch + route removal held traffic away, metrics stabilized near baseline. Handing to oncall-runbook for next 24h watch. :white_check_mark:
